intro: From a week-long Facebook ban in 2010 to a nationwide shutdown on election day 2024 — a look at how access has been switched on and off over 15 years.

facts.heading: The First Big Ban (2010)
facts.detail: Facebook, YouTube, Wikipedia, and Flickr were banned over a controversial page deemed blasphemous, with the ban lifted after roughly a week.
facts.source: TechJuice — Pakistan's decade-long history of Social Media bans

facts.heading: Three Years Without YouTube
facts.detail: YouTube was blocked nationwide, alongside roughly 20,000 other websites, after the 'Innocence of Muslims' film sparked protests in September 2012. Access wasn't restored until January 2016, after Google launched a localized, filterable version.

facts.heading: PECA Becomes Law (2016)
facts.detail: The Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act gave the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority formal legal power under Section 37 to block and remove online content — a legal foundation still used today.
facts.source: Freedom House — Freedom on the Net 2022

facts.heading: Protest-Triggered Blackout (2017)
facts.detail: In November 2017, YouTube, Twitter, and Facebook were suspended nationwide during protests over a change to a lawmakers' oath. A court later ruled a related mobile shutdown illegal.
facts.source: Freedom House — Freedom on the Net 2018

facts.heading: TikTok Banned (2020)
facts.detail: TikTok was banned nationwide for 'immoral content' — part of a wider pattern of platform-specific restrictions distinct from broader network shutdowns.

facts.heading: Election Day Shutdown (2024)
facts.detail: On 8 February 2024, mobile internet and phone services were suspended nationwide on general election day itself. X (Twitter) was banned nine days later, with the government only publicly confirming the block in April, citing 'national security'.
facts.source: Digital Rights Foundation — Annual Report 2024; Dawn

facts.heading: A National Firewall?
facts.detail: Through mid-to-late 2024, reports emerged — later partly confirmed — of a national internet 'firewall' system being tested for traffic monitoring and content blocking, alongside a controversial (later rescinded) mandatory VPN registration proposal.

facts.heading: The Economic Cost
facts.detail: According to VPN-reviewer Top10VPN.com, Pakistan topped the world in financial losses from internet and social-media outages in 2024, with national internet speeds falling among the lowest 12% globally that year.
facts.source: Dawn — 'The year they came for the internet', Usama Khilji
